sections.overview: The Double-striped Tabby is a European pyralid moth, recorded in Britain as locally common in southern counties.
sections.habitat: Adults visit haystacks and thatched buildings.
sections.diet: Larvae feed in hay, thatch and other dry plant matter.
sections.behavior: Adults fly in July and August and come to light.
sections.reproduction: The cited account describes larvae but gives no full breeding schedule.
sections.ecology: Bird nests are also reported as larval feeding sites.
sections.conservation: UKMoths suggests local numbers are decreasing in southern England.
